ocr.page-010:
Prologue
Inception

The sun was setting over a vast warm ocean,
reflecting the purple and orange hues of the sky
above, as the late evening bats began to emerge from
the forest. Ducking and weaving through the air, they
flew against the mesmerizing sunset catching the
evening feast of mosquitos that danced around them.
The evening air was warm, and a gentle breeze moved.
the tall silk curtains adorning the large balcony of the
stunningly modern oceanfront property.

In the distance, the last small boats of evening
fishermen returned to the shore with their catches of
the day. There, on the sea front balcony, a man waited
alone, tanned by the Caribbean sun, and dressed in
ocr.page-011:
linen for comfort. He looked on at the small boats
with admiration, mixed with a little envy at the
simplicity of their work compared to the complexity
of his own craft. Nevertheless, he respected the labor
the fishermen expended to land their catch. Through
his shaded glasses, the colors of the orange and purple
sky were muted, however he had seen these hues
every night for the last few years, and he appreciated
the natural beauty of the sunset before him.

Shifting slightly in his chair, the man cast a gaze
towards the town, where the local port nestled in
the sandy shoreline. As the sun was drawing down,
the lights of the town began to sparkle in the dusk
light. Larger yachts docked at the port, with crewmen
loading supplies and fuel for their onward journeys to
neighboring islands and farther beyond the horizon.
His open laptop glowed gently as it rested on his
lap, his design finally complete after over a year of
studious and dedicated work.

While the laptop fan hummed desperately on his
lap trying to cool itself, the man starred out to
the large white hulls of the yachts in the distance,
which were a stark contrast to the faded and cracked
ocr.page-012:
exteriors of the small fishing boats. Their vast hulls
gleamed against the darkening waters around them.
The small port had grown in popularity over the
years, and there must have been at least fifty yachts
moored there now, all of them jostling in the late
evening waters. Some of the boats were at least fifty
to sixty feet long, enough to house several luxurious
bedrooms and lounge areas. The man looked on and
wondered if any new yachts would be able to fit in the
small port; there were likely to be more arrivals in the
next few years due to the turmoil around the world.

While he sat, pondering his existence and the
world before him, a woman watched the scene unfold
from behind the veil. This was her world, and he was
the architect of her designs. The view was exactly as
she remembered it. This was the last time she would
see this place, yet she must finish what she started.

It must be ready.

With a wave of her hand, the clouds departed the
sky, revealing the bright orange glow of the setting
sun in all its glory. She emerged from the house to
take in the fullness of her surroundings.

“Are you ready?” she asked.
ocr.page-013:
With his concentration broken, he turned to the
woman behind him as she stepped forward and put
her hand calmly on his shoulder, gripping it gently.
She was slender and athletic, aside from the large
bump she carried—pregnant with a baby boy.

“Always,” he said.

His conviction was firm, and the project was
complete. Behind a glassy screen, concealed within
a meticulous coded world, a key lay hidden. It was
not simply a collection of words but a gateway to
something far greater. The man on the balcony had
woven an intricate tapestry that only the astute and
observant could decipher. A cryptographic legacy that
promised wealth and power to the first person able to
unveil its contents. For as long as he was needed, the
architect would be the virtual steward of his master’s
will, and then, when the time was right, he would
reveal her legacy.

The architect, sentient to the significance of his
master’s creation, understood that the discovery of
the key would mark a turning point, an extraordinary
moment that could bridge worlds and break wars.

The moment had come.
